decisions.reason: As a generic utility service rather than a differentiated energy-market solution, it is more likely to fall short of aspiration levels and be discontinued so resources can support the platform-oriented core business.
Because it is close to the firm's database-heavy core offer, management is likely to tolerate some uncertainty and keep it while testing whether the Austrian niche can meet aspiration levels.
This service fits the firm's regulatory and operational energy expertise well, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it unless clear evidence of persistent underperformance emerges.
A tariff database with several models shows stronger commitment and platform fit, making it more likely to be kept as part of the firm's broader standardized data and application portfolio.

Although adjacent to existing capabilities, custom web services are less scalable than the firm's SaaS and modular-platform direction, so management would be more inclined to redeploy resources if returns are not clearly satisfactory.
Like the address tool, this is a relatively generic lookup service with weaker strategic distinctiveness, so it is more likely to be dropped if it does not exceed minimum aspiration levels.
